An equal ball argument in all source ellipsoids proves containment of the ellipsoid with averaged center and averaged positive definite shape in the target section.

Conjugation by A^{-1/2} reduces the two-shape determinant inequality to the product expansion in the positive eigenvalues. The mean over degree-r products is at least the geometric mean of those products, equal to the determinant ratio to power r/d. Degree one is strict for nonconstant eigenvalues in d≥2; all positive scalar shapes are proportional in d=1.

For a finite positive mixture, applying the two-shape bound inductively gives strictness if any pair differs by more than proportional scaling. Equal maximal determinants force equal shapes. At affine-majorant contacts linearity produces the exact upper bound at the integer average, so only proportionality is required.

The averaged ellipsoid has the target's maximal volume, so general John uniqueness identifies its center and shape. Every integer point in the lifted center graph comes from a convex average, giving precisely the stated singleton sections.

dependencies.hypotheses: Its proof establishes ellipsoid existence and uniqueness for any compact convex set with interior, using log-determinant for shapes and a larger ellipsoid in B_d+[-v,v] to exclude different centers. Each source and target section invoked here has a positive-volume ellipsoid.

overlap.comparison: The raw-moment optimizer bases have a stronger integer-free property by strict interpolation in a special moment graph. It gives no equality analysis for arbitrary compact convex graphs or for general positive affine-majorant contacts.
Contains the general existence and uniqueness proof for a single compact convex body, but no integer graph or averaged-shape rigidity.
